reason: The hypothesis relies on the claim that serrated interfaces improve properties, but the cited evidence (E4) only discusses serrated grain boundaries in Ni-based superalloys and a different HEA fabricated by SLM, not serrated lamellar interfaces in eutectic HEAs. E3 and E1 provide no direct support for the serration mechanism or its effect on strength and ductility in the target material. The key premises are therefore largely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Serrated interfaces promote strain delocalization and additional strain hardening
Serrated interfaces can be induced by a tailored post-processing treatment
Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain smooth lamellar interfaces prone to microcracking
Serrated grain boundaries improve tensile properties in other alloy systems
